## Exercises (sample)

1. The servlet input stream is consumed once; without a caching/replaying wrapper the controller sees nothing left.
2. The client typically gets an empty response body even though the controller “wrote” to the wrapper.
3. When you only need URL/method/status/timing or simple header inject/check — no body access.
4. Full-body buffering can exhaust memory; exclude large upload paths or cap size.
5. `ContentCachingRequestWrapper`.

## Self-check

1. `HttpServletRequestWrapper`.
2. **False.** Once committed/flushed, many header changes fail or are ignored.
3. The response body bytes (and related metadata) so you can inspect them and later copy out.
4. **No.** Prefer path limits; logging huge/binary payloads is costly and noisy.
